title: Do the Bits of the Number Alternate?

concept.title: XOR the number with itself shifted by one: alternating bits turn into all ones
body: Does the binary representation of a number consist of bits that **alternate** between 0 and 1, so that no two neighbouring bits are equal? For `5 = 101` yes, for `10 = 1010` yes, for `7 = 111` no, for `11 = 1011` no. The number `1` (a single bit) alternates trivially.

Compare every bit with its neighbour at the same time. The number `x >> 1` is `x` shifted one place to the right: its bit at the position `i` is the bit of `x` at the position `i + 1`. So the bit `i` of `x ^ (x >> 1)` is 1 exactly when the two **neighbouring bits** `i` and `i + 1` of `x` are **different**. If all neighbours are different, `y = x ^ (x >> 1)` is a number whose bits are **all 1**, like `111...1`. A number is all ones exactly when `y & (y + 1) == 0` (adding 1 to `111` gives `1000`, and `111 & 1000 = 0`).

body.code:
for x in numbers:
    y = x ^ (x >> 1)             # 1 where neighbouring bits differ
    answer.append("yes" if y & (y + 1) == 0 else "no")
print(*answer)

body: For `x = 5 = 101`: `y = 101 ^ 010 = 111`, all ones: yes. For `x = 7 = 111`: `y = 111 ^ 011 = 100`, and `100 & 101 = 100`, not zero: no. The highest bit of `y` always equals the highest bit of `x` (it has no neighbour above), which is why the leading ones are handled correctly. The test takes O(1) per number.

statement: For each of the `q` given numbers print `yes` if the bits of its binary representation (without leading zeros) alternate, so that no two neighbouring bits are equal, and `no` otherwise.
inputFormat: The first line has `q`: the number of questions.
outputFormat: Print `q` words (`yes` or `no`) on one line, separated by spaces.

examples.note: 101 and 1010 alternate; 111 and 1011 do not: yes no no yes.

hints: x ^ (x >> 1) has a 1 where two neighbouring bits of x differ.
The bits alternate if this number is all ones.
A number y is all ones when y & (y + 1) == 0.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

q = int(input())
ns = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: x ^ (x >> 1) has a 1 exactly where two neighbouring bits of x differ, so the bits alternate when this value is all ones, which is tested with y & (y + 1) == 0.
